correctness.rationale: Each normalized vector of coordinate sum one determines a unique rank-one symmetric projection; for distinct lines the two products cannot be equal and nonzero, so adjacency is orthogonality. A partial orthonormal frame has nonsingular complement W; it is terminal exactly when W is alternating, equivalently the canonical dot-product vector lies in the frame span. Nonalternating forms over this perfect field diagonalize: a remaining symplectic plane can be absorbed using [1]⊥H≅I₃. As a separate count check, for a nonterminal ordered prefix with residual dimension d there are q^(d−1) norm-one successors. Exactly one is terminal when d is odd (the residual canonical vector), and none when d is even. Thus nonterminal prefixes grow by q^(d−1)−1_{d odd}, which equals G_d/G_{d−1} for d≥2; for d=1 the only successor is terminal. This recovers the two ordered counts G_n/G_{n−k} and G_n/H_{n−k} on their allowed branches, including the zero alternating complement. Division by k! gives unordered cliques; the empty clique is separate and forbidden terms are omitted (G₀ is not used). Verified both n=4 example polynomials and m₂=16, m₄=160, m₆=32 for (6,2). Inspected VERIFICATION.md and verify.py without running them: all-size finite enumeration is configured for ten cases, with literal product checks on six, not a universal or formal certificate.

value.rationale: A natural question for the commuting graph is whether partial commuting families are extendible to maximal cardinality. The alternating complement gives a real obstruction, including isolated vertices or two-vertex terminal families in unbounded dimension. Resolving every terminal size and count together with the full counting polynomial quantifies this phenomenon across all characteristic-two orders; a maximum-clique calculation alone would miss it.
